16.14.20.en: * Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? (Ps 2:105) From death we have become immortal. Have you understood the victory and the way it was reached? Learn how this triumph was acquired without toil and sweat. Our weapons were not stained with blood, we did not stand in the battle line, we were not wounded, we did not even see the battle, yet we have won the battle. The striving is (our enjoyment) of our Christ, and the crown of victory is ours.

16.14.21.en: Since the victory is ours, it is fitting for us as soldiers to chant today with joyful voices the hymns of triumph. Let us praise our Master, saying: [Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy victory? O grave, where is thy sting?] (1 Cor 54:15-55).

16.15.s.en: 3. His recourse to the just God

16.15.0.en: 17 Although there is no injustice in my hands, and my prayer is pure. 18 "O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place. 19 Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high. 20 My friends scorn me: mine eye poureth out tears unto God. 21 That he might judge a man with God, as a son of man with his neighbor.

16.15.1.en: "Although there is no injustice in my hands, and my prayer is pure." [17]

16.15.2.en: The testimony of his conscience remained upright and never left him, for he did not mention that he had committed injustice against any person, nor offered a prayer for temporal things, nor spread out his hands in prayer after defiling them with some injustice.

16.15.3.en: * [There was no injustice in his hand] (Job 16:17). It is said of the Savior in the divinely inspired Holy Scripture: [He had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth] (Isa 53:9), [My prayer was pure], for the Savior was pure even from anger and wrath. It was plain to the Jews who crucified Him that He prayed: "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do" (Lk 23:34). Therefore Job was a prophet and a God-bearer, who by certain words was able to see the sufferings of Christ as though they were before him. For this reason he spoke about his own person with the aim of showing the sufferings to the forefathers of the Jewish people, so that people might be able to understand them well, and afterward He presented to us the very event itself.

16.15.4.en: He did not offer his righteous speech out of boasting, but to lead his friends, and all the generations after them, to follow his example.

16.15.5.en: In his speech he left us a good seal, his pure prayers.

16.15.6.en: They comfort and help the righteous toward purity of prayer, as they are made worthy of faith. They keep prayer pure in the same way that Paul also understands it: [I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting] (1 Tim 2:8). For prayer is pure when the hands are pure from covetousness and from every blemish. Let us know this: how can a man be righteous unless it is by reason of his inner man (Rom 7:22), freed from malice, and not falling into doubt when he prays? For we speak with God Himself, and we draw near to the great King, who washes me thoroughly from mine iniquity and cleanses me from my sin (Ps 51:3).

16.15.7.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * As I remember, I said that the blessed Job, who bears a symbol of the Holy Church, uses at times the voice of the body (the Church), and at other times the voice of the Head (the Lord Christ). And while he speaks of her members, suddenly he speaks with the words of her Head. Therefore he adds here: "I suffered this without iniquity of my hand, while offering my pure prayers to God" (LXX). He suffered without iniquity in his hand, [who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth] (1 Pet 2:22). Yet he endured the pain of the Cross for our salvation. He alone above all others made pure prayers to God, for in enduring the distress of His sufferings He prayed for His persecutors, saying: "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do" (Lk 23:34). How can the purity of prayer be described more than this? Who can understand it more than this?

16.15.8.en: He grants the tenderness of His intercession even to those whose hands practiced the suffering, for the very blood of our Savior, which His persecutors shed in their rage, they came to drink after they believed in Him, declaring that He is the Son of God.

16.15.10.en: * The purity of his prayer arises from these circumstances: it is not unseemly for him to ask for forgiveness in his prayer, since in truth he himself grants pardon to others.

16.15.11.en: St. Augustine * Be moved by prayer, ask for tenderness with humility, and take from the Giver of good things...

16.15.12.en: He is the one who receives all prayers and petitions; no prayer enters to His Father without Him, and no gift comes out from Him except by His hands...

16.15.13.en: He received the prayer of Hannah in the temple of the sanctuary, and went out to her with mercies from His Father's house.

16.15.14.en: He listened to the prayer of Jonah in the belly of the whale, and brought it in to His Father as an offering.

16.15.15.en: He listened to the Pharisee and the publican in the temple of the sanctuary, when they stood up to pray, and heard the petition...

16.15.16.en: He hears the whole world, and does not forget to present its prayers just as they were rendered...

16.15.17.en: * Pure prayer finds its way to God; it speaks to Him, listens to Him and trusts in Him.

16.15.18.en: * Do not grow weary in your asking. Do not think that your petition returns empty.

16.15.19.en: Do not say: I have asked much and have not found, and perhaps I shall never find.

16.16.0.en: St. Mar Jacob of Sarug "O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place." [18]

16.16.1.en: Some interpret this phrase as meaning that he sees his friends to have shed his innocent blood by pouring false accusations against him, so he asks the earth to witness for him against them, and not to confine his cries in any place, but to let them rise to God on high.

16.16.2.en: If his friends have accused him of evil and hypocrisy, then he calls the earth to witness: if he has shed innocent blood or committed some crime, let it uncover it and make it known (Gen 4:10-11; Isa 26), and let it not conceal his soul so that it does not cry out.

16.16.3.en: * "Cover not"; may the struggles of Job not be forgotten, may the very sweat of my distress, which pours forth in the practice of virtue, not be taken away, I who have put on every kind of works of patience. May the sores of the righteous man be uncovered to the eyes of the public, so that they may purify themselves by the desire to imitate him.

16.16.4.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * Remember his pure conscience and his blameless prayer: "O earth, cover not the blood of my body" (Job 16:18) LXX, so that his prayer may be directed like incense toward the Lord (Ps 141:2), and not be deposited in the earth.

16.16.5.en: The prayer of the saint pierces the clouds (Sir 35:17), but the earth opens its mouth and hides the prayer of the sinner in the blood of the flesh, as God said to Cain the murderer: [Now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand; when thou tillest the ground] (see Gen 4:11-12).

16.16.6.en: St. Ambrose * "O earth, cover not the blood of my body, and let my cry find no place in which to hide in thee" (18 LXX). It was said to man when he committed sin: [Dust thou art (earth), and unto dust shalt thou return] (Gen 3:19). [This earth] does not cover the blood of our Savior, where every sinner takes for himself the price of his salvation, and confesses, praises and proclaims it to all his kinsmen as far as he can. Moreover, the earth did not cover His blood, since the Holy Church has preached the mystery of His salvation in all parts of the world.

16.16.7.en: Observe what he adds: [Let my cry find no place in which to hide in thee]. For the very blood of salvation which is received is itself the cry of our Redeemer. Paul says: [The blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel] (Heb 12:24). It was said of the blood of Abel: [The voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground] (Gen 4:10). But the blood of Jesus speaks better things than the blood of Abel, for the blood of Abel brought about the death of his brother, whereas the blood of the Lord gained life for His persecutors. Therefore the mystery of our Lord's passion is not without profit in us, but we are bound to imitate what we receive and to preach what we worship.

16.17.0.en: "Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high." [19]

16.17.1.en: Lest he be accused anew of being proud and ascribing to himself a self-righteousness, he asks heaven to bear witness for him, and the One who dwells in it to declare his uprightness.

16.17.2.en: * If you ask: And where was witness borne to Him? I answer you: At the Jordan, saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 3:17)...

16.17.3.en: He made clear that there is no voice in God, and no form for Him, but He is higher than all forms and tones of this kind.

16.17.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * [My witness in heaven] not because of his wealth, for God has no need of a reward, He who does not fear works of enmity, and is not occupied with the love of the world (Mt 6:19-20).

16.17.5.en: [And my advocate on high], He who knows best the works and the words and the movements of thoughts, He who gives us the unforgettable memory of Job preserved in the divine Scriptures.

16.17.6.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * [Also behold my witness is in heaven, and the fellowship of my heart on high] (Job 16:19) LXX. For when the Son came down to earth He had a witness in heaven, for the Father is witness to the Son, of whom He said in the Gospel: "The Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me" (Jn 5:37). Rightly also He was called "the fellowship of my heart," since they have one will and one counsel, the Father working always in union with the Son...

16.17.7.en: This can also apply to the voice of His body, the Holy Church, which bears the tragedies of this life for the sake of the heavenly grace that leads her toward the eternal rewards.

16.17.8.en: She despises bodily death, as she aims toward the glory of the resurrection. What she suffers is temporary, and what she expects is eternal. She has no doubt concerning these eternal blessings. For she sees with the mind the resurrection of His body, and is greatly strengthened to have hope, and reckons that what she has seen has passed through her Head. And she hopes without doubt that it will be fulfilled in His body, that is, in her...

16.17.9.en: So may the believing people, when they suffer from opposition, when they are troubled by bitter afflictions, lift up their mind to the hope of the glory to come, and trust in the resurrection of the Redeemer, saying: "Even now I see my witness in heaven, and the fellowship of my heart on high."

16.17.10.en: Rightly He called Him "fellowship," since He has known our nature not only by creating it, but also by taking it to Himself. His knowledge was fulfilled by taking what is ours...

16.17.11.en: But this voice can apply to each one of us along with the blessed Job, for every man who aims in what he does at human praise seeks a witness on earth. But he who longs by his deeds for the good pleasure of Almighty God thinks that he has a witness in heaven.

16.17.12.en: It often happens that the good works themselves in us are reckoned sinful by rash people, but he who has a witness in heaven has no need to fear the reproaches of men.

16.17.14.en: * When the wise obtain good things, they send a part of them ahead of them, as Job said: [My witnesses in heaven] (Job 16:19). And also: [My brothers and my beloved are with God] (Job 16:20). And our Lord commands those who gain possessions to make for themselves friends in heaven out of them, and to lay up for themselves treasures there.

16.18.0.en: mine eye poureth out tears unto God." [20]

16.18.1.en: His friends did not stop at opposing him, but began to defame him and conspire against him. He expects from them neither kindness nor comfort, but pours out his tears before God alone, the source of all comfort, offering Him the sacrifice of a broken and contrite heart, which He does not despise! The friends mocked his cries, so he offered his tears as a pure offering to God, in hope of relief for the weary.

16.18.2.en: * [Let my petitions come before the Lord]. For if my prayer reaches on high, my enemies perish (Ps 91:2); the righteous stands firm (Wis 5:1), the snare is broken, and the bird, set free, flies in liberty (Ps 124:7); and the persecutors bow their heads, while the persecuted rejoice (Mt 5:10-12).

16.18.3.en: * [And let mine eyes weep before him]. He said deliberately [before him], that is, before God. Job added this fittingly, for weeping before men is of no benefit at all to those who pray. For even if they adorn themselves with wise thoughts, it is madness for us to receive glory from men.

16.18.4.en: But let us pour out our tears before Him (Ps 56:8), for as much as we let our tears overflow in prayer before the Lord, the deceitful flee and are dissolved (Ps 5:6), while the King is clothed with tenderness.

16.18.5.en: For tears wash souls and bodies, and cleanse every defilement, and wholly purge every blemish, and make those who weep appear whiter than snow (Ps 51:7-9).

16.18.6.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * "My friends are full of words, but mine eye poureth out tears unto God" (LXX). What does he mean by the eye but the intention of the heart? "If therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light" (Mt 6:22).

16.19.0.en: "That he might judge a man with God, as a son of man with his neighbor." [21]

16.19.1.en: Job knows that there is no man who can judge in his favor, but he stands before God, the searcher of hearts, who knows the thoughts and intentions; He alone can judge him and so justify him through His rich grace.

16.19.2.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem sees that the man referred to here is the Son of Man, the Son who became incarnate for our sake (Jn 1:12; Rom 3; 1 Jn 4:2; 2 Jn 7), who sits at the right hand of the Father (Ps 110:1). He intercedes for us as equal to the Father in royal honor, and refutes the accusations of the devil who slanders us.

16.20.0.en: "When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return." [22]

16.20.1.en: Job felt that death was at the doors; a few years would pass, and he would enter his eternal home, and would no longer return to this world.

16.20.2.en: * [My years are numbered, and their end is coming] (Job 16:22), meaning that I do not ask this in vain, but because the end of my life has been reached, and the collapse of that life is near...!

16.20.3.en: [I am going the way of no return], of which David said: [I go the way of all the earth] (1 Kgs 2:2).

16.20.4.en: To return here, that is, below, is impossible for man. The prophet David himself testifies concerning his son who died, saying: "I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me" (2 Sam 12:23). On the other hand, since we are going on a road after which it is impossible to return here, let us hasten and prepare provision for the journey, that is, the virtues. On this road we shall neither hunger nor thirst, nor be stripped nor lose the glory of life.

16.20.5.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem Job realized that the Messiah would not come in his time. The life of Abbot Sisoes the Great tells how the true believer rejoices at the moments of his soul's departure from this world, even though, in his sense of weakness, he asks for a chance to remain for repentance. It was said of him that when he was about to leave the world he said: "Behold, Father Anthony is coming." After a little he murmured, saying: "Behold, the ranks of the prophets have come," then he said: "The ranks of the apostles are coming." And each time his face shone more brightly. At one moment he seemed to be speaking with someone, and those present asked him: "Who is it that speaks with you, Father?" He said: "Behold, I see the angels who have come to receive my soul. But I entreated them to give me a little time that I might repent." The elders said to him: "You have no need of repentance, Father." The old man said to them: "In truth, I do not think that I have even begun yet." Then all were convinced that he was at a very high stature of holiness and perfection. His face shone like the sun, and those present were afraid, but he declared to them: "Behold, the Lord has come, and He says: Bring me the vessel of the wilderness." And at once he gave up his spirit, and there was in the place something like lightning, and the whole house was filled with a sweet fragrance."

16.20.6.en: Since the Lord has broken the power of death and has shone upon us with the splendor of His resurrection, the believers weep, not for fear of death for themselves or for their loved ones, but rather they weep over their sins, as they weep out of longing to depart and be with the Lord Christ.

16.20.7.en: * As, according to the natural order, we weep for the dead, so it is fitting for us to weep for our salvation, in a manner that cannot be surpassed.

16.20.8.en: Let us weep with such longing and courage that everything may serve us... Let us remember salvation.

16.20.9.en: Those who lose their children and wives think of nothing but those they have lost, while we who have lost a heavenly kingdom think of anything but this.

16.20.10.en: There is no man who loses his father (or his mother or one of his relatives) who is ashamed to submit to the law of mourning, even if he is of royal descent. For he falls to the ground and weeps bitterly, and changes his garments, and of his own will does all the things that befit such a time.

16.20.11.en: This is not done as a result of training, nor out of weakness belonging to such grief, but he does all this without any difficulty... But we who grieve, not for a wife, nor for a child, but for a soul, not for another, but for our own souls, make an excuse for ourselves on the plea of poor health or of our being people of high learning...

16.20.12.en: Yet we neglect even what requires no bodily effort.

16.20.13.en: I ask: what effort do we need in order to practice contrition of heart, vigil in prayer, and reflection on our sins...? These are the things that make God merciful toward us. But we do not do such things.

16.20.14.en: St. John Chrysostom The author of the life of St. Ephrem the Syrian, ascribed to St. Gregory of Nyssa, depicts for us how he was concerned to shed tears in order to enjoy eternal salvation.

16.20.15.en: [When I began to recall the flood of his tears, I myself began to weep, for it was very difficult to pass with dry eyes through the ocean of his tears.

16.20.16.en: There was never a day or a night, or a part of the day or the night, or any moment, however short, in which his watchful eyes were not seen swimming in tears.

16.20.17.en: And as he said, at times he wept for the misery and folly of all in general, and at times he wept for certain vices. You would find him weeping and lamenting not only when he spoke of repentance, ethics and the disciplining of life, but even during the prayers of praise.]

16.20.18.en: * The soul is dead through sin. This calls for grief, weeping and tears, mourning and lamentation over the iniquity that brought it down to destruction.

16.20.19.en: Crying, weeping and lamenting bring it back to God...

16.20.20.en: God grieves over the image that was lost (because of our sins). The soul is much dearer to God than all His creation. Through sin it has become dead, and you, O sinner, do you not care...?!

16.20.21.en: Pour out tears and raise it up!

16.20.22.en: Offer God this joy; He rejoices that you are raising up your soul.

16.20.23.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian * Let us have pity on ourselves, and open a way to the righteous tenderness of the Father! Let us sow in tears, that we may reap in joy!

16.20.24.en: * Tears are the flood that falls upon sins, and they cleanse the world.

16.20.27.en: * Often I long to hear a word of comfort from a man.

16.20.28.en: But I have realized that they are all miserable comforters.

16.20.29.en: There is none who can enter my depths, and share my feelings, and groan with my groanings, except You, O Lover of every human soul!

16.20.30.en: They may utter sweet words with their lips, but do they have a heart wide enough to bear my weaknesses?

16.20.31.en: And even if they speak gentle words, the eyes of man criticize, whereas Your eyes behold all that is good and beautiful in me!

16.20.32.en: * Grant me not to lean on human consolations; You are my reliance, my comfort and the joy of my heart.

16.20.33.en: Even if You wound me, Your wounds carry a medicine for my healing.

16.20.34.en: With Your chastenings I feel the surpassing sweetness of Your love!

16.20.35.en: * Grant me, in the midst of my sufferings, not to be preoccupied with the looks of people or their words.

16.20.36.en: But let me look to You, O Source of all comfort!

16.20.37.en: * Let the sons of men make light of me, for in their mockery I see a useful medicine for my depths!

16.20.38.en: Let me bear all mockery, for You alone shine upon me, and scatter my darkness, O Sun of Righteousness.

16.20.39.en: * I marvel: if people are silent, I feel their neglect of me.

16.20.40.en: And if they speak, they pierce my heart with their words as with deadly arrows!

16.20.41.en: But You, in Your silence, carry me to the vision of Your glories, and in Your words, You kindle my heart with Your love!

16.20.42.en: Teach me how to be silent, and how to speak!

16.20.43.en: Let the law of Your love be the guide of my silence and my words!

16.20.44.en: * Let me carry You in my depths, and present You to my brethren, present You to them by my prayers for them, and by my words that carry the sweetness of Your love!

16.20.45.en: Let me present to them not the arrows of criticism that tears down, but the arrows of Your love, which, though they wound, heal!

16.20.46.en: * Your comforts to me are the declaration of Your presence within me!

16.20.47.en: I see You, O Crucified One, and I find the pain sweet even unto death!

16.20.48.en: I see You destroying by the Cross the power of the devil, and I realize that the opposition of the enemy of good is only for my victory.

16.20.49.en: Let him strike with all his might, for I am hidden in You.

16.20.50.en: In You I enjoy a crown of glory that does not fade!

16.20.51.en: * My enemy who bears witness against me opens for me the door of victory over him!

16.20.52.en: It is a war that does not cease, but what can the devil do to You, O my Savior?

16.20.53.en: Can darkness put out the light?

16.20.54.en: Can the antichrist usurp Your Kingdom?

16.20.55.en: What a petty enemy he is!

16.20.56.en: He is deceitful and malicious, but You are the Truth that cannot be resisted!

16.20.57.en: * In the midst of my affliction let me open my eyes and see You, and if You allow chastening, You are a Father.

16.20.58.en: And if the affliction becomes extremely severe, Your eyes have pity on me!

16.20.59.en: The devil has no authority over me!

16.20.60.en: He may distort my image and press me hard!

16.20.61.en: But You are the secret of my eternal splendor and my heavenly rest!

16.20.62.en: * The enemy of good wants to strike me on my cheek, so that I may not utter a word of witness for You.

16.20.63.en: But Your word in my mouth is a blazing fire.

16.20.64.en: The enemy will not be able to quench its flame, nor can he silence it!

16.20.65.en: * Truly the enemy of good is like a dangerous giant; he will not despair of warring against the Church as a whole, and against every member in her.

16.20.66.en: He began his war with the first man in Paradise, and he continues to wage war in all generations in various ways, and will not stop until the end of the ages.

16.20.67.en: He works with all his might through the antichrist!

16.20.68.en: He works with all deceit and cunning, seizing every opportunity to destroy us!

16.20.69.en: He turns our life into hell, so that we lose hope of our salvation!

16.20.70.en: He darkens our eyes with despair, and we think that death has taken us captive forever!

16.20.71.en: But Your death has granted us the resurrection, and Your ascension has opened the gates of heaven before us!

16.20.72.en: The devil will no longer be able to imprison us in Hades, where there is eternal darkness!

16.20.73.en: We shall no longer fear him, for You, O Redeemer, are our victory!

16.20.74.en: You are our resurrection and our crown!

16.20.75.en: * Let the enemy strike with all his might, for the earth itself cries out.

16.20.76.en: The earth will not accept to drink innocent blood, but cries out to You.

16.20.77.en: The earth could not hold You in the tomb, for You are the Heavenly One.

16.20.78.en: Let me be united with You, so that I may no longer return to the dust of the earth, but in You become heavenly, and enjoy the fellowship of the heavenly glories.

16.20.79.en: * In the midst of my sufferings I see You as a witness for me in heaven!

16.20.80.en: You bear witness for me by Your death, Your resurrection and Your ascension, for as I share Your sufferings, I enjoy the fellowship of Your glories!

16.20.81.en: * In the midst of my sufferings my tears pour forth, not before people, but before You.

16.20.82.en: For men are miserable comforters, but You cherish my tears!

16.20.83.en: * In the midst of my sufferings I await my passing over to You.

16.20.84.en: My years are few, and the end of my earthly life is coming.

16.20.85.en: I am going the way of all the earth!

16.20.86.en: But not alone, for You are with me!

16.20.87.en: And to You I go to rest forever!
